turns.t: G'day, doctor. Now, my daughter Kerry reckons I've been forgetting things, and I said it's just old age, but she insisted, so here I am. Lovely clinic, by the way, I like the plants.
Thanks, they're my pride and joy. What kind of things are you forgetting?
Oh, names. Where I put my keys. Last week I went to the shops for milk and came back with biscuits and no milk.
How long has this been going on?
Six months, Kerry says, she keeps a diary on the fridge.
Do you ever get lost, even in places you know? ~
No, never. I know every street in this suburb. ~
Any falls?
No, no falls.
Any headaches?
No headaches.
Any low mood?
No, I'm a cheerful sort.
What do you take?
A cholesterol tablet, atorvastatin, maybe 20 mg, once a day. I'd have to check with Kerry.
Anything for your memory, anything you've bought from the chemist? ~
No. Just the one. ~
Any health conditions?
High cholesterol, and migraines when I was young.
Let me check you. Pulse 70, blood pressure 134 over 80.
Good for a man of seventy-eight? ~
Very good. Now I'm going to give you three words to remember, and I'll ask you in a minute. Apple, table, penny.
Apple, table, penny. Got it. ~
Now, can you tell me today's date and where we are? ~
Wednesday, the, er, fourteenth? And this is the medical centre on Station Street. ~
Close. It's the fifteenth. And now, the three words? ~
Apple. Table. And, er, what's the third, a coin... penny? ~
Yes. So you recalled all three, but needed a hint for one, and you were out by one day on the date.
Is that bad? ~
It's not alarming, but I'd like to look further. Any trouble with your balance, or weakness?
No, nothing like that.
Here's what I'm thinking. It could be nothing more than stress or poor sleep, but I can't rule out the early stages of a memory problem.
Alzheimer's? ~
I'm not saying that. It's early days. I'd like to arrange blood tests, including vitamin B12 and thyroid, since both can affect memory.
Right. ~
And I'd like to arrange a proper memory assessment at the memory clinic.
How long's the wait? ~
A few weeks. And I'd like to start vitamin B12, 1000 micrograms, once a day, in the meantime.
Okay. ~
Keep a notebook for the things you forget, and bring it along.
Kerry will love that. ~
Good. That's all for now. ~
Thanks, doctor. ~
